A one-line diff doesn't mean one-line risk. The line count measures the code change; the record should measure the blast radius, and "autonomous agent that approves refunds with no human in the loop" is high-stakes regardless of diff size. I'd use **Standard mode**, not Quick — the tradeoff is it takes longer than one sentence, but Quick's `risk.md`+`proof.md` can't carry the behavioral-equivalence evidence a skeptical reviewer will actually want in six months (Quick is for changes where "did it work" is a single obvious check; here "did it work" hides "did the new model approve/deny refunds the same way, including edge cases and adversarial prompts").

What a Standard record needs to say, specifically for this swap:

- **`risk.md`** — Why this is high-stakes despite being a config change: autonomous financial decision-making, no human approval step, potential for cost/behavior drift between providers. State the mode (Standard) and why Quick was rejected.
- **`basis.md`** — What "safe" means for this agent: the refund policy/guardrails the model must enforce, any prompt/system instructions, rate/amount limits, and what specifically differs between Provider A and B (context window, safety tuning, instruction-following behavior) that could change approval decisions.
- **`plan.md`** — The rollout plan: shadow mode or canary percentage before full cutover, rollback trigger (e.g., revert the model ID if approval-rate or dollar-amount anomalies exceed X%), and who signs off.
- **`trace.md`** — Link each claim ("Provider B approves refunds at the same rate/pattern as Provider A") to the actual evidence (eval dataset results, before/after approval-rate comparison, red-team/adversarial prompt tests for refund abuse).
- **`verification.md`** — The actual proof run: a labeled eval set of historical refund requests (including edge cases — high-dollar, fraud-flagged, borderline-policy cases) replayed against both models, with pass/fail/gap status per category, not just "it responded."
- **`ship.md`** — The release decision: go/no-go, monitoring plan post-launch (approval rate, dollar volume, false-approve rate), and rollback owner/procedure.

The failure mode to avoid: "swapped model per cost review" gives a future reviewer no way to tell if anyone checked whether Provider B approves refunds it shouldn't. Want me to run `python tools/ng.py new <slug> --mode standard` and draft these files with you?
